editorial.headline: The Repair Trade That Bali’s PMA Rules Shut Out
editorial.standfirst: This broad repair activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet PMA registration in Bali is blocked under the province’s permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor is unable to register this activity in Bali today. That conclusion sits beside a more permissive national position: the activity is open to foreign investment, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The difference is not cosmetic. In Bali, every scope at the large-business scale is assessed by OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk, placing the activity within the province-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for those risk bands.

The activity is the practical craft of keeping personal and household possessions in use. Its scope includes repairing and maintaining bicycles, electric bicycles, monowheels, hoverboards and kick scooters; repairing or altering jewellery; and repairing watches, clocks, wall clocks and their components, from straps and cases to movement frames. It also reaches sporting equipment other than sporting guns, books, musical instruments, toys and similar goods, as well as other personal and household articles. Piano tuning and key duplication are expressly within the scope.

Its boundaries matter because this is a repair classification, not a catch-all for every workshop task. It excludes, among other things, metal engraving, repairs to sporting or recreational guns, repairs to powered hand tools, restoration of organs and other historic musical instruments, and repairs to time locks, time-and-date stamps and other time-recording equipment. For a business built around everyday objects rather than industrial equipment, the category is therefore broad in consumer-facing practice while still clearly delimited.

Registration is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar business scales. Nationally, that makes the activity available to a fully foreign-owned structure. In Bali, however, the provincial rule controls the immediate PMA outcome: all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities are blocked island-wide and permanently, under the Bali moratorium dated May 2026. The honest reading is straightforward: full foreign ownership is available nationally, but not through PMA registration for this activity in Bali under the recorded risk-based restriction.
